answer: Picture a meadow of honest agents; a sybil farm wants to flood it like a rising tide. The defense: each new identity must solve a fresh, memory-hard admission puzzle seeded by its own public key, then broadcast the solution as its join signal. Because the puzzle is memory-bound, a farm cannot amortize it across GPUs or bulk-buy shortcuts, so every extra fake agent pays its own full RAM-seconds: a thousand sybils cost a thousand independent solves, not one.
